{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Re-load the data to ensure consistency
trial = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Final check: confirm the response variable is binary (1/0)
print("Response variable (responded) values:")
print(trial['responded'].value_counts())

# Cross-tabulation of sex and treatment arm
print("\nCross-tabulation of sex and treatment arm:")
treatment_by_sex = pd.crosstab(trial['sex'], trial['arm'])
print(treatment_by_sex)

# Compute response rates by sex and arm
response_by_sex_arm = trial.groupby(['sex', 'arm'])['responded'].mean().unstack(level='arm')
print("\nResponse rates by sex and arm:")
print(response_by_sex_arm)

# Compute within-arm differences in response rate (F - M)
within_arm_diff = response_by_sex_arm['treatment'] - response_by_sex_arm['control']
print("\nWithin-arm difference in response rate (F - M) by arm:")
print(within_arm_diff)

# Compute weighted average difference across arms
n_control = trial[trial['arm'] == 'control'].shape[0]
n_treatment = trial[trial['arm'] == 'treatment'].shape[0]
weighted_sex_effect = (
    (n_control * (response_by_sex_arm.loc['F', 'control'] - response_by_sex_arm.loc['M', 'control'])) +
    (n_treatment * (response_by_sex_arm.loc['F', 'treatment'] - response_by_sex_arm.loc['M', 'treatment']))
) / (n_control + n_treatment)

print(f"\nWeighted average difference in response rate (F - M) across arms: {weighted_sex_effect:.4f}")"}
